requirements.text: Change the background into a basketball court
requirements.source_phrase: Change the background into a basketball court

outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Do the visible court markings belong to a sufficiently broad, continuous playing surface that reads as a basketball court across the background, rather than a narrow floor strip beneath a mostly featureless wall?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the playing surface and markings make the background read as a basketball court across a substantial visible area; fail if basketball equipment or isolated lines are present but most of the background remains non-court; unknown if the surface or its extent cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Assess the edited background directly, using the source image as context for the requested background change. Distinguish the extent of the court setting from basketball equipment alone; do not infer from other support answers. A fail does not erase other basketball-related progress.

nodes.question: Does the background show recognizable basketball-court markings or basketball equipment?
nodes.criteria: Pass if recognizable court markings or basketball equipment are visible in the background; fail if neither is visible despite an assessable background; unknown if the background cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Look for court markings or basketball equipment in the background as evidence that it is a basketball court. This evidence does not alone establish complete fulfillment.

nodes.question: Do the visible court markings and playing surface together make the background read as a coherent basketball court, rather than isolated court features against a predominantly featureless backdrop?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the background’s visible surface and markings together form a recognizable basketball playing area; fail if court features are isolated and the background does not read as a court; unknown if the surface or its relation to the markings cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Assess the background as a whole, not merely the presence of a hoop, ball, or isolated line. A pass supports completion; a fail does not erase basketball-related progress evidenced by other supports. Do not treat ambiguity as a negative.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete only when s1 and s3 support a recognizable basketball-court background; s2 alone, including equipment or isolated markings, establishes at most progress. Partial when s2 or other support evidence shows basketball-related progress but s3 fails to establish a coherent court background. Absent when supports show no requested progress. Unknown when necessary evidence is unresolved; do not infer visual facts beyond the supports.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks overlap and contradict one another in scope: s1 and s3 both assess whether the background reads as a coherent court across a substantial area, while s2 treats either markings or equipment as progress. The fulfillment rule then requires both s1 and s3 for completion, duplicating the same extent condition rather than composing distinct evidence. More importantly, s1 can fail because the court occupies too little of the background, yet s3 can pass on a recognizable playing area without requiring substantial coverage; the readout does not resolve that conflict and could mark completion despite s1’s known incompleteness. The requested background replacement is otherwise represented, but the composition rules do not faithfully distinguish complete fulfillment from partial progress."}
